idiom_name: plain POJO service behind a thin servlet or framework controller (JUnit 5 + Mockito)
implementation_notes: Java's replacement for the humble class is the plain object: move the decisions into a POJO service with constructor-injected collaborators and leave the servlet or controller with the request plumbing - read the parameters, call the service, write the response. JUnit 5 drives the service directly, and Mockito verifies the shell's delegation when the shell itself is tested; the servlet lifecycle (container threads, init and destroy callbacks) is precisely why that shell stays out of the unit tests. Keep the framework code where it genuinely implements container behaviour (transactions, security, session), but move any decision it carries into the service.
pitfalls: Container-managed threading: the servlet runs on a container thread, so a Mockito verify executed inside an answer on that thread may never be observed by the test thread; verify after the call returns or assert on observable state.
Mocking the framework (request, response, session) instead of extracting the logic produces brittle tests tied to container behaviour; confine framework interaction to the few remaining shell tests.
One validation left in the servlet makes the request the only path that exercises the rule; the service tests stay green while the real behaviour is untested.
